title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a compliance failure at the physical layer of a data center deployment, not a failure of a model or its outputs. The facility's power equipment was installed and run without the permits New Jersey requires for installation or operation, and state inspectors found it that way. The failure sits in the gap between a site being built and a site being authorized to run.

Catching it would have taken a permit review before the generators were installed and again before they were operated, which is a paperwork and inspection step rather than a technical one. The campus is partly in use while construction continues, so the equipment was in service before the state's inspection in late July. Noise complaints from homeowners and violation orders from the county health department point to the same period of operation.

What is not established: the federal lawsuit over noise is an allegation, not a verdict, and the reporting does not establish that the operator knew permits were required or intended to skip them. Nothing in the reporting establishes that any AI system or model was involved in the violation.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators at its Vineland data center construction site in late July. The generators, each rated at 2,000 kilowatts and about the size of a tractor trailer, lacked required permits to be installed or operated. Officials said the penalty for violating the Air Pollution Control Act is the largest ever issued to a New Jersey data center operator.

The Vineland campus is planned as a 2.6 million square foot complex needing 350 megawatts, enough to power a medium size city, and is slated for completion at the end of the year. Some of it is already in use. Homeowners have filed a federal lawsuit over persistent noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department issued violation orders for excessive noise. Governor Mikie Sherrill said data center development must benefit New Jersey communities.
